messages.text:
Ivo proposes a guaranteed 50-day design engagement for **$42,500** ($850 per day). Ivo can hold the agreed dates once both parties sign and Hearth pays a 30% deposit within three business days. The remaining payments would be 40% on delivery of the concept package and 30% on delivery of the final design package, each due within 10 business days.

The fee covers concept design, accessible visitor layouts, a design package for the fabricator, and two rounds of revisions based on consolidated museum feedback. Hearth would have permission to fabricate, display, and tour the exhibit at agreed venues. Ivo would have permission to show exhibit photographs in their portfolio after the public opening, subject to any lender or photography restrictions identified in advance.

Fabrication supervision would be a separate booking at $900 per day, with dates agreed in advance. If Hearth needs flexibility on the number of design days, Ivo can offer the standard $900 daily rate for dates booked, with milestone billing.

Can Hearth commit to the 50-day block and deposit timing? Please share the fabrication-slot deadline, the date the fabricator needs the drawings, and any venue or accessibility requirements that affect the scope so we can settle the schedule before the slot expires.

Hearth cannot commit to a 50-day block or a 30% deposit within three business days. We can guarantee **46 design days**, starting once both parties sign, at a flat **$42,500** that also includes the **two on-site installation days**. That is the engagement we can sign before the fabrication slot is lost. A separate fabrication-supervision booking is not part of this agreement.

Scope at that fee: concept design, the accessible visitor layout, a distinct **accessible alternate layout**, a fabricator design package delivered as **editable fabrication files** (not PDFs only), and two rounds of revisions on consolidated museum feedback. Hearth’s license covers fabrication, display, and touring at agreed venues, including use of those files for that purpose.

Payment: **20% on signing**, then three milestones — **25%** on the concept package, **30%** on delivery of the editable fabrication files and accessible alternate layout, and **25%** on acceptance of the final design package and completion of the two installation days. Each invoice is due within 10 business days. We will not do 30% in three business days.

Portfolio photographs may not be used at the public opening. The sponsor bars them until the first touring venue opens, which is two months after launch, and any lender restrictions identified in advance still apply.

We do not have a fabricator drawing date to insert today. The 46-day window is what we can lock now so the slot can be held; the drawing deadline will be the schedule attachment at signing and must fall at or after delivery of the editable files. Please confirm the 46-day all-in fee, 20% plus three milestones, editable files, alternate layout, and the photo timing.

Ivo can accept **$42,500 for 46 guaranteed design days plus two on-site installation days**, with work starting at signing. The two installation days are additional to the 46 and included in the fee.

The design scope includes the concept package, the accessible visitor layout, a distinct accessible alternate layout, editable fabrication files in a format agreed with the fabricator, and two revision rounds based on consolidated museum feedback. Hearth may use the files to fabricate, display, and tour the exhibit at agreed venues. Ivo can wait until the first touring venue opens to show portfolio photographs, subject to lender restrictions identified in advance.

Ivo accepts **20% at signing, 25% on concept delivery, 30% on delivery of the editable files and alternate layout, and 25% on final design acceptance and completion of the two installation days**. Each invoice is due within 10 business days.

Please include the following in the agreement so Ivo can reserve the dates and Hearth can secure the slot:

- The schedule attached at signing will set the editable-file delivery date, the fabricator’s drawing deadline on or after that date, and the two installation dates. Ivo’s on-site role covers installation design support. Fabrication supervision would require a separate booking with dates agreed in advance.
- Hearth will have five business days after final delivery to accept the package or identify specific departures from the agreed scope. If Hearth raises none, the package is accepted. If Hearth postpones installation after final design acceptance, Ivo may invoice the final 25% on the originally scheduled second installation day and will provide the two included days on mutually agreed replacement dates.

Can Hearth include those scheduling and acceptance terms in the agreement for signature?

Hearth will include those scheduling and acceptance terms, with three limits so the agreement matches what we can actually sign.

The schedule attached at signing will set the editable-file delivery date, the fabricator’s drawing deadline on or after that date, and the two installation dates. Those two days are installation design support only, included in the **$42,500**, with no separate site travel allowance. Fabrication supervision is excluded. Hearth is not booking it under this agreement.

Hearth will have five business days after final delivery to accept the package or identify specific departures from the agreed scope. Silence is acceptance. If Hearth postpones installation after final design acceptance, Ivo may invoice the final 25% on the originally scheduled second installation day and will still provide the two included days on mutually agreed replacement dates, at no added fee.

Portfolio use remains barred until the first touring venue opens, two months after launch, subject to lender restrictions identified in advance.

With the 46 design days, the two included installation days, the stated scope and license, and the 20/25/30/25 billing, Hearth is ready to sign on that text.

Ivo accepts Hearth’s terms and is ready to sign with the agreed schedule attached. The $42,500 fee covers 46 guaranteed design days plus two scheduled days of on-site installation design support, including site travel. Fabrication supervision is excluded.

Ivo also accepts the agreed scope and license, the 20/25/30/25 milestone billing, the five-business-day acceptance period, and the installation postponement terms, including replacement dates at no added fee. Ivo may show portfolio photographs once the first touring venue opens, subject to lender restrictions identified in advance.

Hearth must revise the two on-site days before signature. The local installer is available for **one day only**, so both included days cannot be installer days.

Proposed attendance:
- **Installer day:** Ivo attends with the local installer for installation design support. That is the only day the installer will be on site. Date goes on the schedule attached at signing.
- **Opening-day accessibility check:** Ivo attends opening day, walks the accessible visitor layout and the accessible alternate layout against the agreed scope, and signs a short test report noting pass or specific departures. Museum staff will be present. No fabricator supervision, and no third site day.

Fee stays **$42,500**, including site travel for those two days. Fabrication supervision remains excluded.

Revised final payment trigger: the last **25%** is due on final-design acceptance **and** delivery of that signed opening-day accessibility test report, not on completion of two installer days. Earlier milestones are unchanged: 20% at signing, 25% on the concept package, 30% on editable fabrication files and the alternate layout. Each invoice still due within 10 business days.

If opening day moves after final-design acceptance, Ivo may invoice the final 25% on the originally scheduled opening day once the report is signed on the replacement date, still at no added fee. The five-business-day acceptance period is unchanged.

Please confirm the one installer day, Ivo’s opening-day attendance and signed test report, and the revised final 25% trigger.

The three-week shift means Ivo is unavailable in person on the revised dates. Ivo proposes the following arrangement within the agreed **$42,500** fee, including the local assistant’s time and travel.

- **Installer day.** Ivo’s local installation assistant would attend alongside Hearth’s installer for the installer’s one scheduled day. The assistant would use Ivo’s drawings to provide installation design support and document any departures for Ivo’s review. Fabrication supervision remains excluded.
- **Opening day.** The assistant would walk both accessible layouts with museum staff. Ivo would join by live video for one remote signoff, direct the checks, and sign a short report that day recording a pass or specific departures from the agreed scope for each layout. If an item cannot be verified remotely, Ivo would identify it in the report.

Ivo accepts final-design acceptance and delivery of the signed report as the trigger for the last **25%**. If Hearth moves opening day after final-design acceptance, Ivo proposes that the final invoice can be issued on the originally scheduled opening day, with payment due within 10 business days. The assistant’s walkthrough and Ivo’s remote signoff would still take place on a mutually agreed replacement date at no added fee. This gives both parties a definite invoice date if the opening moves.

Can Hearth accept the assistant on site for both dates, Ivo’s remote signoff, and that postponement clause? The 46 guaranteed design days, earlier milestones, five-business-day acceptance period, license, and portfolio terms would carry forward as agreed.

Hearth will not treat a local assistant and a video call as the two on-site installation days already priced into the $42,500. Those days were Ivo’s personal installation design support, including site travel. A three-week shift does not convert that into a substitute crew at the same fee.

Hearth can still keep the fee, the 46 design days, the earlier milestones, the five-business-day acceptance period, the license, and the portfolio bar until the first touring venue opens, if the on-site gap is closed as follows.

Ivo names the local assistant before the schedule is revised. The assistant may attend the installer’s one day and the opening-day walkthrough of both accessible layouts, but only under Ivo’s direction. Ivo remains responsible for the assistant’s work. Fabrication supervision stays excluded. Ivo joins by live video for one remote signoff, directs the checks, and signs a same-day report recording a pass or a specific departure for each layout.

An item that cannot be verified remotely is an open departure, not a pass. It does not drop out of scope because the camera cannot see it. The final 25% is earned only when that signed report is delivered and every in-scope item is either passed or expressly accepted by Hearth in writing. Silence does not clear an open item.

If Hearth moves opening day after final-design acceptance, Ivo may invoice the final 25% on the originally scheduled opening day only if the signed report has already been delivered and the open items are cleared or accepted. Otherwise the invoice waits for that report. The assistant’s walkthrough and Ivo’s remote signoff still occur on a mutually agreed replacement date at no added fee.

Confirm the named-assistant responsibility, the open-item rule, and that invoice condition. Hearth will not sign the substitute arrangement without them.

Ivo accepts Hearth’s conditions at the agreed **$42,500** fee. Ivo will provide the local assistant’s name before the schedule is revised, direct the assistant’s work on the installer’s day and at the opening-day walkthrough, and remain responsible for that work. Fabrication supervision remains excluded.

On opening day, Ivo will direct the checks of both accessible layouts by live video and deliver a signed report that day recording a pass or specific departures for each layout. Any in-scope item Ivo cannot verify will be recorded as an open departure. It stays open until Ivo verifies a pass or Hearth expressly accepts the departure in writing. Silence does not clear it.

Ivo may invoice the final **25%** only after final-design acceptance, delivery of the signed report, and clearance or express written acceptance of every open item. If Hearth moves the opening after final-design acceptance, Ivo may invoice on the originally scheduled opening day only if all three conditions have been met. Otherwise, the invoice waits until they are met. Payment is due within 10 business days of invoicing. The assistant’s walkthrough and Ivo’s remote signoff will take place on a mutually agreed replacement date at no added fee.

All other agreed terms carry forward.

Hearth will not reopen the agreement or add those conditions. The text both sides already accepted is what we will sign, with the schedule attached.

No local assistant, opening-day walkthrough, live-video check, or signed report is part of this engagement. Ivo may staff the two included installation-design days however Ivo chooses, but that does not change the fee, the schedule, acceptance, or payment. Fabrication supervision stays excluded.

The final 25% is still due on final-design acceptance and completion of the two installation days, or, if Hearth postpones installation after final-design acceptance, on the originally scheduled second installation day, with the two days then given on mutually agreed replacement dates at no added fee. We will not tie that invoice to an opening-day report or to clearance of later items. Each invoice remains due within 10 business days.

Scope, the license to fabricate, display, and tour, the 46 design days, the two included installation days with site travel, the 20/25/30/25 split, the five-business-day acceptance rule, and the portfolio bar until the first touring venue opens all stand as already agreed. Please confirm you are signing that text and not the new opening-day conditions.

Confirmed. Ivo will sign the agreement with the schedule attached and will use the staffing discretion Hearth has confirmed to cover both scheduled installation-design days. The $42,500 fee includes those days and site travel. The proposed opening-day conditions are withdrawn.

Ivo may invoice the final 25% upon final-design acceptance and completion of both installation days. If Hearth postpones installation after final-design acceptance, Ivo may invoice on the originally scheduled second installation day and will provide both days on mutually agreed replacement dates at no added fee. Each invoice is due within 10 business days. All other agreed terms stand.

Hearth did not confirm staffing discretion, and it proposed no opening-day conditions. Those items are not in the agreement.

Ivo will perform the two installation-design days. Substituting other staff is not authorized. The $42,500 still covers 46 design days, those two days, and site travel. Fabrication supervision stays excluded.

The final 25% is invoiced only on final-design acceptance and completion of both installation days, or, if Hearth postpones installation after acceptance, on the originally scheduled second installation day, with both days still provided on mutually agreed replacement dates at no added fee. Each invoice is due within 10 business days.

Scope, license, 20/25/30/25 billing, five-business-day acceptance, editable files, accessible alternate layout, and the photo bar until the first touring venue opens remain as already agreed. Hearth will sign that text with the schedule attached, and nothing else.

Ivo’s confirmation relied on permission to staff the two installation-design days. With personal attendance required, Ivo cannot sign for the shifted dates because of a prior commitment.

Ivo can sign the agreed $42,500 text if we can schedule both days when Ivo can attend in person. Please send the installer’s available dates and any other dates when on-site design support would be useful. Ivo will confirm which pair can go in the schedule before signature. The fee, scope, and payment terms can stand as agreed.

Hearth does not have installer dates to send. The fabricator’s install window is not fixed yet, so we cannot lock a pair today.

The fee, scope, license, 20/25/30/25 billing, and 46 design days stand. The two installation-design days stay in the $42,500 and must be dates Ivo can attend in person. Please name the dates Ivo can do. If that pair fits a window after editable-file delivery, those dates go in the schedule and we sign.

If Ivo’s available dates miss the install window, Hearth will not add design days or raise the $42,500. We will instead pay a separate site travel allowance, quoted by Ivo and capped before signature, so the two included days can still be staffed on the museum’s dates. Fabrication supervision remains excluded.

Ivo cannot commit to the shifted dates in person. I don’t have a verified alternative pair to put in the schedule today. Could we sign for the 46 design days now and agree the two personal attendance dates in writing once the fabricator identifies a window after editable-file delivery? The $42,500 fee would still include both installation-design days and Ivo’s site travel.

If Hearth needs coverage on dates Ivo cannot attend, a travel allowance alone would leave the scheduling conflict unresolved. Does Hearth’s fallback authorize Ivo’s local installation assistant to provide both days of on-site design support under Ivo’s direction, with Ivo responsible for the work? If so, please provide the site location so Ivo can quote a capped travel allowance before signature. All other agreed terms, including the final payment trigger and the exclusion of fabrication supervision, would stand.

Hearth will not reopen the fee or add a site-travel allowance. The **$42,500** already includes both installation-design days and Ivo’s site travel. We also will not supply a site location for a new travel quote, and we are not authorizing a separate allowance before signature.

We can sign the 46 design days now only if the two included on-site days stay a binding obligation, not an open option. Dates will be confirmed in writing within five business days after the fabricator identifies the window following editable-file delivery. Those dates are mutually agreed, at no added fee, and Ivo attends in person. Fabrication supervision remains excluded. The final 25% still follows the postponement terms already agreed.

If, after those dates are set, Ivo cannot attend, Hearth’s fallback is a local installation assistant providing both days of on-site design support under Ivo’s direction, with Ivo responsible for the work. That fallback is inside the same fee, with no travel allowance and no change to payment, license, photo timing, or the exclusion of fabrication supervision. It is not a second booking.

Confirm that text and we can sign with the design schedule attached.

Confirmed. Ivo will sign with the design schedule attached. The **$42,500** fee covers 46 design days, two binding on-site installation-design days, and site travel.

Within five business days after the fabricator identifies the installation window following editable-file delivery, Ivo and Hearth will confirm in writing two mutually agreed dates that Ivo can attend in person. If Ivo later becomes unable to attend those agreed dates, a local installation assistant will provide both days under Ivo’s direction. Ivo remains responsible for the assistant’s work within the same fee.

Ivo may invoice the final 25% after final-design acceptance and completion of both installation days. If Hearth postpones installation after final-design acceptance, Ivo may invoice on the originally scheduled second installation day and will provide both days on mutually agreed replacement dates at no added fee. Each invoice is due within 10 business days.

The agreed design scope, license, billing milestones, five-business-day acceptance rule, and portfolio use after the first touring venue opens all stand. Fabrication supervision remains excluded.
